name: Fruit sandwiches

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Prepare the filling
① Hull the strawberries. Peel the bananas
and cut each into four pieces. Peel the kiwi
and cut into eight pieces.
② Add the sugar to the cream and whip to
medium-stiff peaks. Add the mascarpone
and continue whipping until stiff peaks
form.

Assemble the sandwiches
① Spread cream 2-② on one side of each slice of cocoa
sandwich bread (about 35 g for the bottom slice and 25 g for
the top).
② Arrange the strawberries, banana and kiwi on the bottom
slice and cover with the top slice.
③ Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate.
• Plain bread may be used instead.
• You can use different kinds of fruit.

3

2

1,446 kcal per loaf (including
filling)

Program 5: Sandwich bread

Fruit sandwiches

Method

Make the cocoa sandwich bread using Program 5.

① Fit the kneading blade in the bread pan, add A, and place the
pan in the machine.
② Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser, select Program 5 and
press Start.
③ When baked, remove the loaf from the pan.
④ When cool, cut into about 10 slices (do not use the end slices).

1

* At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use cold water (about
5°C) and reduce it by 10 g (mL).

Ingredients

Cocoa sandwich bread
<A>
Bread flour ... 230g
Butter ... 10g
Sugar ... 25.5g(3 large spoons)
Skim milk powder ... 6g(1 large spoon)
Salt ... 5g(1 small spoon)
Baking cocoa ... 18g(3 tbsp)
Water * ... 170g(mL)

Dry yeast ... 2.8(1 small spoon)

Filling
Cream ... 200g(about 200mL)
Sugar ... 17g(2 large spoons)
Mascarpone 50g
Strawberries ... 16pieces (240g)
Banana ... 2pieces (240g)
Kiwi ... 1egg (120g)

name: Smoked salmon sandwiches

ingredients.name: Celery, thinly sliced across the fibres

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Prepare the filling
① Lightly rub the celery with salt and drain.
② Put the coarsely mashed boiled eggs in a bowl, add the
mayonnaise and mix well. Season with salt and pepper.

Assemble the sandwiches
① Spread one side of each slice of potato sandwich
bread with softened butter (not included in the
quantities).
② Add the smoked salmon, mixture 2-②, celery 2-①
and dill, in that order.
③ Top with another slice of potato sandwich bread and
press lightly.

3

name: Pain de campagne (with poolish)

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Program 11: French bread
Pain de campagne
(made with poolish)

Ingredients
900kcal

Poolish (pre-ferment)
<A>
Water (about 25°C) ... 100g(mL)
Dry yeast ... 0.7g(¼ small spoon)
Bread flour ... 100g

<B>
Bread flour ... 100g
Wholemeal flour ... 50g
Salt ... 5g(1 small spoon)
Cold water (5°C) * ... 90g(mL)

Dry yeast ... 1.4g(½ small spoon)

* At room temperatures of 25°C or
above, reduce the amount by 10 g
(mL).
Using a poolish takes a little more effort, but produces an authentic
pain de campagne. Do not use the delay timer when using a poolish.
For a simpler version, use the quantities given for the recipe without
poolish.

Without poolish (pre-ferment)

Bread flour ... 200g
Wholemeal flour ... 50g
Salt ... 5g(1 small spoon)
Cold water (5°C) * ... 190g(mL)
Dry yeast ... 1.4g(½ small spoon)

* At room temperatures of 25°C or
above, reduce the amount by 10 g
(mL).

Fit the kneading blade in the bread
pan and add all ingredients except
the dry yeast. Put the dry yeast in the
yeast dispenser. Select Program 11
and press Start.

Method

1 Make the poolish (pre-ferment)
① Put the water and dry yeast in a bowl and whisk to dissolve.
② Add the bread flour and mix with a rubber spatula until smooth,
with no dry flour remaining. The finished poolish should be 20–30°C.
③ Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a plastic bag. Leave at room
temperature for 60 minutes, then refrigerate for 8–18 hours.

2 Bake using Program 11
① Fit the kneading blade in the bread pan. Add B and the poolish A,
then place the pan in the machine.
② Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser, select Program 11 and press
Start.

3 Remove the loaf
Lay a towel underneath. Move your hands firmly downwards,
tapping against the work surface to release the bread. See
“French bread” in the instruction manual.

notes: Follow the recipe-specific preparation and corresponding instruction-manual program. The complete source excerpt preserves all conditions and method details.

Do not use the delay timer with poolish. Leave the poolish at room temperature for 60 minutes, then refrigerate for 8–18 hours. Use only the with-poolish ingredients; the source page also shows a separate without-poolish alternative.

name: Cinnamon rolls

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Method

1 Make the dough using Program 17
① Fit the kneading blade in the bread pan, add A, and place the
pan in the machine.
② Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser, select Program 17 and
press Start.
2 Remove the dough (finish the work within 15 minutes!)
① When the machine beeps, open the lid, remove the dough from the bread pan,
and remove the kneading blade.
• Do not press Cancel.
3 Roll out
① Roll the dough into a rectangle about
15 cm deep × 25 cm wide.
4 Shape
① Brush the nearest three-
quarters of the dough with milk.
Sprinkle with cinnamon sugar
and scatter over the dried fruit.
② Roll up from the edge nearest
you.
③ Cut into four equal lengths
and place in the bread pan.

5 Bake
(Press Start again.)

6 Make the icing
① Put B in a bowl and stir over a 60°C water bath to make the icing.

7 Finish
① When baked, remove the bread from the pan and drizzle with icing.

When making custom bread…

Keep the combined weight of dough and filling to
600 g or less!
• Too much filling may prevent the bread from
rising or baking through.
Avoid fillings with a high moisture content!
(Reduce their moisture by simmering, for
example, and let them cool to room
temperature.)
• They affect dough fermentation.

Prepare the filling in advance!
• You have 15 minutes to work.

name: Sweet bean bread

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
What if the dough
is sticky and
difficult to roll out?

Dust your hands
and rolling pin with
bread flour to
make rolling
easier.

Q
A

Method

1 Make the dough using Program 17
① Fit the kneading blade in the bread pan, add A, and place the pan in the
machine.
② Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser, select Program 17 and press Start.

2 Remove the dough (finish the work within 15 minutes!)
① When the machine beeps, open the lid, remove the dough from the bread pan,
and remove the kneading blade.
• Do not press Cancel.

3 Roll out
① Roll the dough into a long rectangle (about 8
cm × 30 cm). Keep it narrower than the bread pan.

4 Add the filling and shape
① Spread the sweet bean paste evenly over the dough,
leaving a border of about 1 cm to prevent it from spilling over.
② Roll up from the edge nearest you without trapping air, and
seal the seam firmly.
③ Place in the bread pan, seam-side down.

5 Bake
(Press Start again.)

Program 17: Custom bread

Sweet bean bread

Ingredients
1148kcal(one item )

<A>
Bread flour ... 180g
Butter ... 15g
Sugar ... 17g(2 large spoons)
Skim milk powder ... 6g(1 large spoon)
Salt ... 2.5g(½ small spoon)
Egg, beaten ... 25g(½ medium egg )
Cold water (5°C) * ... 110g(mL)

Dry yeast ... 2.1g(¾ small spoon)
Sweet bean paste (at about 20°C) ...
100g
* At room temperatures of 25°C or above, reduce
the amount by 10 g (mL).
• More bean paste will reduce the rise (maximum 150
g). Always keep the paste at about 20°C, as its
temperature affects fermentation.
• A gap forms between the dough and the paste

because the bread dough expands as it rises.

name: Crème d’Anjou-style dessert

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Program 31: Milk jam
Crème d’Anjou-style dessert

Ingredients
804kcal

Milk jam ... 100g
Plain unsweetened yogurt
(drained) ... 160g
Water ... 30g(mL)
Gelatin ... 3g
<A>

Frozen blueberries ... 50g
Lemon juice ... 7.5g
Granulated sugar ... 25g

① Drain 300 g plain yogurt in the refrigerator overnight
until reduced to about half its weight (160 g).
② Put the water and gelatin in a heatproof container.
Microwave uncovered at 700 W for 30 seconds.
③ Mix the milk jam, drained yogurt and gelatin
mixture. Refrigerate for 1–2 hours until set.
④ Put A in a heatproof bowl and microwave
uncovered at 700 W for 2 minutes.
⑤ Remove, stir and microwave for another minute.
⑥ Spoon mixture ③ into dishes and pour ④ over it.

• To make milk jam, see “Milk jam” in the instruction

Marmalade

Ingredients
697kcal

Amanatsu (summer oranges, oranges, etc.)
→ Wash well and separate the peel from the
flesh.
→ Remove the membranes and divide each
segment into 2–3 pieces.
→ Remove the white pith from the peel and
cut the peel into thin strips.
... 400 g

① Put the peel in a saucepan with enough
water to cover it and boil for about 15
minutes.

③ Repeat three times, then drain.
④ Add the peel, sugar and fruit to the bread
pan, in that order.
⑤ Set the pan in the machine.

Program d5: Pizza dough
Pizza

Ingredients (two pizzas, about 25 cm in diameter)
803 kcal per pizza

Pizza dough (see manual): 1 batch
Bread flour ... 280 g
Shortening ... 15 g
Sugar ... 8.5 g (1 large spoon)
Salt ... 5 g (1 small spoon)
Water ... 180 g (mL)
Dry yeast ... 2.8 g (1 small spoon)
Soy-milk white sauce
Rice flour (without wheat) ... 10 g (1
large spoon)
Soy milk ... 100 g
Bouillon powder ... 1 g
Salt ... a little
Toppings (example)
Onion, thinly sliced ... 60 g
Frankfurters, sliced diagonally 5 mm
thick ... 160 g (10 medium)
Broccoli, cut into bite-sized pieces ...
100 g
Cherry tomatoes, halved ... 120 g
Sweetcorn ... 60 g

To make the soy-milk white sauce
① Put all ingredients in a saucepan.
Heat over medium heat for 2 minutes,
stirring occasionally.
② When the surface begins to bubble,
reduce to low heat and cook for 2
minutes.
③ Remove from the heat when
thickened.

How to make pizza (p. 36)

steps.text:
Dough d1: White bread dough
Domed White Loaf

Ingredients (12 × 12 × 12 cm loaf tin) 1,198 kcal per loaf

White bread dough (see
manual): 1 batch
Egg wash (beaten egg): as
needed

Method

1
Make white bread dough using dough program d1
(see manual).

2
Prove
① Remove the dough from the bread pan. Press
firmly all over, working from the centre outwards, to
expel the gas.
② Fold into thirds, then fold and shape into a ball.
Place in a bowl.
③ Prove at 25–30°C for about 30 minutes, then
remove from the bowl.

3
Shape
① Press all over to expel the gas, then round the
dough into a ball with a taut surface.
② Rest at 25–30°C for 30 minutes. Do not let it dry
out.
③ Roll out with a rolling pin, fold into thirds, then roll
into a log. Pinch the seam firmly closed and place
seam-side down in the loaf tin.
④ Prove at 30–35°C for 40–60 minutes, until the
highest point is level with the top of the tin.

4
Bake
① Brush the surface with egg wash and bake in a
preheated oven at 170–200°C for about 30 minutes.

2- ②

3- ③

name: Sake Lees Bread

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Method

Bake
① Dust with bread flour and press a cross into the top with
cooking chopsticks or a similar tool.
② Bake in a preheated oven at 170–190°C for about 10 minutes.

3

Shape
① Remove the dough from the pan and press gently to expel the gas.
Divide into 4 with a scraper, round with the smooth surface outwards,
and rest at room temperature for about 15 minutes. Do not let it dry out.
② Press all over with your palm to expel the gas. Round into taut balls
with a smooth surface, then pinch the bottoms closed.
③ Prove at 30–35°C for 40–60 minutes, until about twice the original
size.

2

Make white bread dough using dough program d1 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry yeast in
the yeast dispenser and make the dough.
• When the beeper sounds, press Cancel.

name: Matcha and Black Bean Roll

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Dough d1: White bread dough
Matcha and Black Bean Roll

Ingredients 1236 kcal each

A

Bread flour: 200 g
Butter: 15 g
Sugar: 17 g(2 large spoons)
Skim milk powder: 6 g(1 large spoon)
Salt: 3.8 g(¾ small spoons)
Matcha: 2 g(1 tsp)
Egg (beaten): 25 g(½ medium egg)
Cold water (5°C): 110 g(mL)

Dry yeast: 3.5 g(1¼ small spoons)

Method

1
Make white bread dough using dough program d1 (see
manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry
yeast in the yeast dispenser and make the dough.
• When the beeper sounds, press Cancel.

2
Shape
① Open the lid, remove the dough from the pan and remove the
bread blade.
② Roll the dough into a long rectangle slightly narrower than the
bread pan.
③ Scatter the drained black beans evenly over it.
④ Roll up from the edge nearest you.
⑤ Place in the bread pan.
⑥ Prove at [Ferment: 4] for 30–40 minutes, until the dough fills
about 70% of the pan.

3
Bake
① Bake at [Bake: 2] for 35
minutes.

Filling
Sweet simmered black beans: 120
g

Replace the matcha with cocoa powder and roll in chocolate chips
and flaked almonds to make a chocolate-almond roll children will love.

name: Filled Pull-Apart Bread

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Dough d1: White bread dough
Filled Pull-Apart Bread

Ingredients 1,134 kcal (excluding fillings)

A

Bread flour: 200 g
Butter: 35 g
Sugar: 17 g(2 large spoons)
Skim milk powder: 6 g(1 large spoon)
Salt: 3.8 g(¾ small spoons)
Egg (beaten): 25 g(½ medium egg)
Cold water (5°C): 100 g(mL)

Dry yeast: 3.5 g (1¼ small spoons)
Fillings: 12 portions (15 g each)

Method

1
Make white bread dough using dough program d1 (see
manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry
yeast in the yeast dispenser and make the dough.
• When the beeper sounds, press Cancel.

2
Shape
① Open the lid, remove the dough from the pan and remove the
bread blade.
② Divide into 12 with a scraper.
③ Wrap a portion of filling inside each piece.
④ Place in the bread pan.
⑤ Prove at [Ferment: 4] for 30–40 minutes.

3
Bake
① Bake at [Bake: 2] for 35
minutes.

Choose any filling you like (no excess moisture!).
Curry (simmer until the moisture has evaporated), meatballs,
potato salad, sausages, drained tuna, diced cheese, etc.

name: German-Style Sausage Rolls

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Dough d1: White bread dough

Method

German-Style Sausage Rolls

Ingredients (makes 8) 228 kcal each

A
Bread flour: 220 g
Rye flour: 30 g
Butter: 10 g
Sugar: 8.5 g(1 large spoon)
Skim milk powder: 6 g(1 large spoon)
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoon)
Water: 160 g(mL)

Dry yeast: 2.8 g(1 small spoon)

Filling
Sausages: 8
Wholegrain mustard: as needed

To finish
Sesame or poppy seeds (optional): as needed

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so the dough is about
26°C after kneading.

Make white bread dough using dough program d1 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry yeast in the
yeast dispenser and make the dough.
• When the beeper sounds, press Cancel.

1

Shape
① Remove the dough, press gently to expel the gas, divide into 8 with a scraper,
round with the smooth surface outwards and rest at room temperature for about 15
minutes. Do not let it dry out.
② Roll into ovals about the length of the sausages (about 15 cm).
③ Spread wholegrain mustard in the centre and place a sausage on top.
④ Use the scraper to make 5–8 evenly spaced diagonal cuts in the dough on each
side of the sausage.
⑤ Lift the strips from both sides and cross them alternately over the sausage.
⑥ Prove at 30–35°C for 30–50 minutes. A light finger press should leave a slight
indentation.

2

Bake
① Mist the surface with water and
sprinkle with sesame or poppy seeds,
if desired.
② Bake in a preheated oven at 190–
210°C for about 12 minutes.

3

name: Sweet Potato Bread

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Dough d1: White bread dough
Sweet Potato Bread

Ingredients (makes 2) 902 kcal each

A
Bread flour: 250 g
Butter: 15 g
Sugar: 17 g(2 large spoons)
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoon)
Milk: 70 g(about: 70 mL)
Water: 100 g(mL)

Dry yeast: 2.8 g(1 small spoon)
*Black sesame seeds: 13 g

Filling
Sweet potato: 200 g
Water: 150 g (mL)
Sugar: 80 g
Lemon juice: 1 teaspoon

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so the
dough is about 26°C after kneading.

Bake
① Make 4 diagonal slashes in the surface.
② Bake in a preheated oven at 170–190°C for about
15 minutes.

3

Method

Make white bread dough using dough program d1 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry yeast in
the yeast dispenser and make the dough.
• Use the Raisin function (manual addition; see manual): Yes ♪ /
Normal mixing.
* Add the black sesame seeds by hand.
• When the beeper sounds, press Cancel.

1

① Cut the unpeeled sweet potato into small cubes and place in a microwave-
safe container.
② Add the water, sugar and lemon juice, mix well, cover loosely with cling film
and microwave for about 6 minutes, until still slightly firm. Drain and leave to cool.

Preparing the filling

Shape
① Remove the dough, press gently to expel the gas, divide into 2
with a scraper, round with the smooth surface outwards and rest at
room temperature for about 20 minutes. Do not let it dry out.
② Press with your palm into an oval about 25 cm long × 15 cm wide
and scatter the filling over it.
③ Roll up from the edge nearest you and shape.
④ Prove at 30–35°C for 40–60 minutes, until about twice the original
size.

2

name: Walnut and Potato Bread

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Shape
① Remove the dough, press gently to expel the gas, divide into 2
with a scraper, round with the smooth surface outwards and rest at
room temperature for about 15 minutes. Do not let it dry out.
② Press each piece flat and fold into thirds from the near and far
edges.
③ Fold in half again from the folded edge to make a long shape. Seal
the seam firmly and roll into a rope about 45 cm long × 4 cm wide.
④ Use the scraper to cut halfway through the width (about 2 cm)
along one side at roughly 3 cm intervals.
⑤ Join the dough into a ring with the cut sections on the outside.
⑥ Prove at 30–35°C for 30–50 minutes. A light finger press should
leave a slight indentation.

Method

Make white bread dough using dough program d1 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry yeast in the
yeast dispenser and the walnuts in the raisin dispenser, then make the
dough.
• Use the Raisin function (automatic; see manual): Yes / Normal
mixing.
• When the beeper sounds, press Cancel.

Bake
① Bake in a preheated oven at 170–190°C for about 15
minutes.

name: Brown Rice and Honey Bread

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Ingredients (makes
3)

A
French bread flour: 200 g
Brown rice flour: 50 g
Honey: 12 g
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoon)
Water: 170 g(mL)
Dry yeast: 2.1 g(¾ small spoons)

To finish
Brown rice flour: as needed

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so the
dough is about 24°C after kneading.

323 kcal each

Brown Rice and Honey Bread

Method

Make crusty bread dough using dough program d2 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry yeast in
the yeast dispenser and make the dough.
• When the beeper sounds, press Cancel.

1

Shape
① Remove the dough, press gently to expel the gas, divide into 3 with
a scraper, round with the smooth surface outwards and rest at room
temperature for about 15 minutes. Do not let it dry out.
② Press into an oval with your palm.
③ Place the long side horizontally and fold into thirds from the near and
far edges.
④ Fold in half again from the folded edge, press the seam closed, and
roll into a rope about 25 cm long × 4 cm wide.
⑤ Taper both ends.
⑥ Lay a cloth on the kneading board and make a fold at one edge.
Place the dough seam-side down about a finger's width from the fold,
then make another fold on the opposite side.
⑦ Repeat ②–⑥ for the other two pieces.
⑧ Prove at 30–35°C for 30–50 minutes, until about twice the original
size.

2

Bake
① Hold the transfer board at an angle
close beside the dough. With your other
hand, lift the cloth from the opposite side
to turn the dough upside down onto the
board.
② Hold the board beside a sheet of
oven paper cut slightly larger than the
dough. Turn the board over to transfer

board over to transfer the

surface. Place the dough and

Croissants

Can be made with enriched dough or natural yeast bread dough.

Dough d3: Rich dough

Ingredients (12 croissants) • With dry
yeast 201 kcal each

A

Bread flour: 225 g
Cake flour: 55 g
Butter: 15 g
Sugar: 25.5 g(3 large spoons)
Skim milk powder: 6 g(1 large spoon)
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoon)
Egg (beaten): 25 g(½ medium egg)
Water: 140 g(mL)

Dry yeast: 2.8 g (1 small spoon)

thick slices): 140 g

To finish
Egg wash (beaten egg): 25 g (½ medium egg)

Dough d4: Natural yeast dough

• With natural yeast
204 kcal each

A

Prepared natural yeast starter: 25 g(2
large spoons)
Bread flour: 230 g
Cake flour: 50 g
Butter: 15 g
Sugar: 25.5 g(3 large spoons)
Skim milk powder: 6 g(1 large spoon)
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoon)
Egg (beaten): 25 g(½ medium egg)
Water: 120 g(mL)

Butter for laminating (cut into 1
cm-thick slices): 140 g

To finish
Egg wash (beaten egg): 25 g (½ medium egg)

Method

1
Make the dough
With dry yeast: make enriched dough using dough program d3 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry yeast in the yeast
dispenser and make the dough.
With natural yeast: make natural yeast bread dough using dough program d4 (see
manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add the prepared starter, then A. Make the
dough.

2
Laminate with butter
① Remove the dough, place in a bowl, cover with cling film and refrigerate
for 30–60 minutes (longer in a warm room).
② Dust the laminating butter with flour, arrange the slices together, wrap in
cling film and roll into a square about 20 × 20 cm. Refrigerate for 15–30
minutes.
③ Press the dough with tapping motions of the rolling pin, then roll into a
square about 30 × 30 cm.
④ Place the butter from ② on the dough and enclose it. Wrap in cling film
and refrigerate for 10–20 minutes.
⑤ Tap with the rolling pin and, once slightly thinner, roll flat.
⑥ Fold into thirds, wrap in cling film and refrigerate for 10–20 minutes.
⑦ Repeat ⑤ and ⑥ twice more, then chill for 30–60 minutes.

3
Shape
① Divide into 2 with a scraper. Roll each piece into a rectangle about 18 ×
40 cm and cut into 6 isosceles triangles.
② Roll up while pulling the ends.
③ Arrange seam-side down.
④ Mist with water, cover with cling film and prove at room temperature for
40–60 minutes, until about twice the size.

4
Bake
① Brush with egg wash and bake in a preheated oven at 200–220°C for
about 10 minutes. Refrigerate the remaining dough to prevent
overproving.

Dough d3: Rich dough
Chocolate Cornets

① Put the egg yolks in a bowl and whisk. Add the

prevent scorching.
⑤ When glossy and falling in a stream from the

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Melon Buns

Ingredients (makes 8) 331 kcal each

① Beat the room-temperature butter with a wooden
spatula or similar until creamy.
② Add the sugar in 2–3 batches, beating each time
until pale and smooth.
③ Add the egg gradually in 3–4 batches, beating after
each addition. Add any flavouring after the egg.
④ Add the sifted cake flour and gently fold with a
cutting motion until no dry flour remains.
⑤ Once the dough comes together, place in a plastic
bag, flatten and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes.
⑥ Remove about 30 minutes before use and let soften
at room temperature.
⑦ Divide into 8 pieces and round each one.

Making the cookie dough
See the variation recipes in the
instruction manual.

Method

Make enriched dough using dough program
d3 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A.
Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser
and make the dough.
• When the beeper sounds, press Cancel.

1

Shape
① Remove the dough, press gently to
expel the gas, divide into 8 with a scraper,
round with the smooth surface outwards
and rest at room temperature for about 15
minutes. Do not let it dry out.
② Press all over with your palm to expel
the gas. Round into taut balls with a smooth
surface and pinch the bottoms closed.
③ Flatten each piece of cookie dough into
a circle slightly larger than the bread dough.
④ Place it over the bread dough to cover
the top completely, then shape.
⑤ Coat the cookie-dough surface with
granulated sugar and mark a grid with the
scraper.
⑥ Prove at 30–35°C for 40–50 minutes,
until about twice the original size.
• Allow the surface to become slightly dry
while proving.

2

Bake
① Bake in a preheated oven at 170–
190°C for about 10 minutes.

3

A
Bread flour: 200 g

Cookie dough

Cake flour: 180 g

• You may flavour the dough with melon oil, vanilla
essence, grated lemon zest or similar, to taste.

To finish
Granulated sugar: 30 g

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so the dough is about
26°C after kneading.

name: Pizza

steps.title: Prepare and weigh
steps.text: Fit the kneading blade in the bread pan. Weigh the dough ingredients exactly. At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use cold water (about 5°C). Keep pizza sauce, cheese and toppings reserved for later. [Instruction Manual pp.18, 76; Recipe Book p.36]

steps.title: Load the bread pan and yeast dispenser
steps.text: Put flour and the other dough ingredients, except dry yeast, in a mound at the centre of the bread pan. Pour water around the edges. Fit and lock the pan in the appliance. Put dry yeast in the dry yeast dispenser. Close both lids. [Instruction Manual pp.18, 76]

steps.title: Select dough program d5 and start
steps.text: Use Dough to select d5, then press Start on the bread maker. Confirm here only after you have performed this machine action. The dough cycle is approximately 45 minutes. [Instruction Manual p.76]

steps.title: Respond to the machine’s completion beeps
steps.text: Wait for the bread maker’s beeps. Press Cancel on the machine and remove the dough immediately; it will continue to rise if left in the pan. This website does not detect the beeps. [Instruction Manual p.76]

steps.title: Divide and rest
steps.text: Divide into 2 with a dough scraper and round with the smooth surface outwards. For thinner pizza bases, the recipe permits dividing into 3. Cover with a cloth and rest for 10–20 minutes. [Recipe Book p.36]

steps.title: Shape and top
steps.text: Place on baking parchment and roll into circles about 25 cm across. Prick with a fork. Spread with pizza sauce, arrange the suggested toppings and add the pizza cheese. [Recipe Book p.36]

steps.title: Bake in your oven
steps.text: Bake in a preheated oven at 180–200°C for about 15 minutes. Refrigerate the remaining dough to prevent overproving. Follow your oven’s operating instructions. Confirm completion yourself. [Recipe Book pp.22, 36]

steps.title: Finish and clean
steps.text: After use, unplug the bread maker and allow it to cool before cleaning. Wash the bread pan and kneading blade as directed; do not immerse the appliance body. [Instruction Manual pp.5, 86–87]

notes: The machine makes the dough only. Shaping, resting, topping and baking in a separate oven are required.
The listed toppings are the source’s suggested toppings, not invented substitutions.
The optional three-base division is documented; ingredient quantities remain unchanged.
Machine actions and completion must be confirmed by you.
otherTime: Rest 10–20 min; external oven bake about 15 min at 180–200°C. Hands-on preparation time unspecified.

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
White Bread

Ingredients 1160 kcal per loaf

A
(Add to the bread pan in the listed
order.)
Dry yeast: 2.8 g(1 small spoon)
Bread flour: 250 g
Sugar: 17 g(2 large spoons)
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoon)
Skim milk powder: 6 g(1 large spoon)
Water: 180 g(mL)

After initial kneading
Butter: 10 g

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so the dough is about 26°C after kneading.

Method

1
Make the dough and give it the first prove
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A in the listed order.
② Initial kneading: [Knead: 1] 2 min → [Knead: 3] 2 min →
[Knead: 4] 10 min (14 min total).
③ Add the butter and knead again: [Knead: 2] 2 min →
[Knead: 3] 2 min → [Knead: 4] 8 min (12 min total).
④ Prove at [Ferment: 3] for about 50 minutes, until about
twice the original size. Remove the dough and take out the
bread blade.

2
Second prove
① Press gently to expel the gas, fold into thirds both horizontally and vertically,
gather together and return to the bread pan.
② Prove at [Ferment: 3] for about 20 minutes, then remove from the pan.

3
Third prove
① Round the dough into a ball with a taut surface.
② Prove at [Ferment: 3] for about 20 minutes, then remove from
the pan.

4
Shape
① Gradually expel the gas with a rolling pin while rolling into an
approximately 18 × 18 cm square. With the smooth side down, fold in one
third, turn, and fold in one third again.
② Turn 90 degrees and roll from the far edge towards you, keeping the
surface taut. Seal the seam firmly.
③ Return to the pan seam-side down and prove at [Ferment: 4] for 40–60
minutes, until the highest point is about 2 cm above the pan.

5
Bake
① Bake at [Bake: 2] for 35
minutes.

name: Custard Buns and Pains aux Raisins

ingredients.name: Brioche dough (make using steps 1-2 on the right)

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Custard Buns (makes 6)

Pains aux Raisins (makes 6)

Ingredients
470 kcal per custard bun
485 kcal per pain aux raisins

Brioche dough
(make using steps 1-2 on the
right): 1 batch
Beaten egg for glazing: as
needed

Filling for pains aux raisins
Raisins: 30 g

Custard
Milk: 250 g(about 250mL)
Egg yolk: 2 pieces
Sugar: 75 g
Cake flour: 25 g
Vanilla essence: as needed

Method

1 Divide the brioche dough
1 On a generously floured board, fold the dough into thirds and
press it to an even thickness. Divide in half with a dough
scraper.

2 Make the custard buns
1 Divide one half into 6 pieces with a dough scraper. Place on
a cloth-lined board and cover with a plastic bag. Rest at room
temperature for about 20 minutes, until evenly warmed and
soft.
2 Round each piece to make the surface taut. Pinch the bottom
firmly closed. Leave at room temperature until pressing with a
finger leaves a slight indentation.
3 Place seam-side up and press with your palm to release the
gas. Roll out to a circle about 10 cm across.
4 Place custard on the dough. Bring the centres of the two
opposite edges together, then seal firmly around the outside.
5 Make three cuts from the sealed edge. Prove at 30-35°C for
50-70 minutes. Guide: a light finger press should leave a slight
indentation.
6 Brush with beaten egg and bake in a preheated oven at
180-200°C for about 10 minutes.

3 Make the pains aux raisins
1 Flatten the other half with your palm and roll into a square
about 20 × 20 cm.
2 Brush off excess flour. Place smooth-side down. Roll the 2
cm strip along the near edge thinner.
3 Spread custard over the dough, leaving the thin strip clear.
Scatter with raisins and brush the thin strip with water.
4 Gradually roll from the far edge towards you. Seal the final
edge firmly.
5 Roll gently to make the log an even thickness. Cut into 6
with a dough scraper and shape. Place in foil baking cases
and press down to an even height.
6 Prove at 30-35°C for 30-50 minutes. Guide: a light finger
press should leave a slight indentation.
7 Brush with beaten egg and bake in a preheated oven at
180-200°C for about 14 minutes.

Making the custard
1 Heat the milk in a saucepan until just below boiling.
2 Whisk the egg yolks in a bowl. Add the sugar and whisk until pale.
3 Lightly mix in the cake flour. Gradually add the hot milk to loosen the
mixture.
4 Strain back into the saucepan.
5 Cook over medium heat, stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to
prevent scorching.
6 When glossy and loose enough to drip from the spoon, remove from
the heat and add the vanilla essence.
7 Spread in a tray, cover with cling film to prevent the surface drying,
and cool.

2

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Brioche

Ingredients (12 brioche moulds, 8 cm diameter)
149 kcal each

Method

1 Make the dough
1 Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A.
2 Initial kneading: [Knead 1] 2 min → [Knead 3] 3 min →
[Knead 4] 10 min (15 min total).
3 Add the butter. Knead again: [Knead 2] 2 min →
[Knead 3] 2 min → [Knead 4] 8 min (12 min total).
4 [Rise 3]: about 30 min, until about 1.5 times its original
size.

2 Refrigerated rise
1 Remove the dough from the pan and press all over to flatten it.
2 Stretch into a round and fold into thirds. Turn it and fold into
thirds again.
3 Place smooth-side up in a tray and press flat. Put in a plastic
bag and let rise in the refrigerator (5°C) for 8-24 hours.

3 Divide the dough
1 Remove from the refrigerator. On a generously floured board,
fold into thirds and press to an even thickness. Divide into 12 with a
dough scraper.
2 Place on a cloth-lined board and cover with a plastic bag. Rest at
room temperature for about 20 minutes, until evenly warmed and
soft.
3 Round each piece to make the surface taut. Pinch the bottom
firmly closed. Leave at room temperature until pressing with a
finger leaves a slight indentation.

4 Shape
1 Place on the board with the seam to the side. Roll back
and forth to form a narrow neck about two-thirds of the way
from the seam.
2 Lift by the neck. Place the larger portion in a brioche
mould, press the smaller portion into its centre, and arrange
the moulds on a baking tray.
3 Prove at 30-35°C for 40-60 minutes. Guide: a light finger
press should leave a slight indentation.

5 Bake
1 Brush with beaten egg and bake in a preheated
oven at 180-200°C for about 12 minutes.

A

French bread flour: 250 g
Sugar: 25.5 g (3 large spoonfuls)
Skim milk powder: 6 g (1 large
spoonful)
Salt: 5 g (1 small spoonful)
1 egg + 1 egg yolk + cold water
(5°C), combined: 160 g
Dry yeast: 4.2 g (1½ small
spoonfuls)

After initial kneading
Butter*: 80 g
To finish
Egg wash (beaten egg): as
needed

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so
the dough is about 24°C after
kneading.
* Cut into 1 cm cubes. Wrap in cling
film or similar, keeping the cubes
separate. Place in an airtight container
and freeze for at least 10 hours.

Black sesame seeds: 30 g

Hulled white sesame seeds:
as needed

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so

Method

1 Make the dough and give it its first rise
1 Fit the bread blade in the pan. Add A and make the dough.
[Knead 1] 2 min → [Knead 3] 3 min → [Knead 4] 15 min (20 min
total).
2 Remove the dough from the pan. Work in the filling evenly by
hand. Form a smooth, taut ball and put it in a lightly oiled bowl.
3 Let rise at about 30°C for about 40 minutes.

2 Second rise
1 Remove the dough from the bowl and press gently to
release the gas. Fold into thirds horizontally, then vertically, to
shape it. Return it to the bowl.
2 Let rise at about 30°C for about 30 minutes.

3 Shape (15 cm logs)
1 Remove the dough from the bowl and divide into 3 with a
dough scraper. Round into smooth, taut balls. Rest at 25-30°C
for about 15 minutes; do not let them dry out.
2 Press all over with your palm to release the gas. Place
smooth-side down, fold in the far third and press together.
3 Turn 180 degrees. Fold in the far third again and press
together. Fold the dough in half and press firmly all over to seal.
• For the sesame version, moisten the dough surface on a
damp cloth, then coat with hulled white sesame seeds.
4 Place seam-side down on a baking tray. Prove at 30-35°C for
about 45 minutes.

• Spray with water beforehand. If your appliance has a
steam function, use it.

4 Bake
1 Make five slashes 2-3 mm deep with a bread lame. Spray
with water.
2 Preheat the oven to 220°C, then reduce to about 170°C and
bake for about 18 minutes.
• If available, use steam for the first 3 minutes for greater
volume and a glossy surface.

name: Baguette-style Bread

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Baguette-style Bread

Ingredients (2 loaves)
461 kcal per loaf
A (add to the pan in the order listed)
French bread flour: 250 g
Malt powder: 1 g
Water: 190 g (mL)

After
initial
kneading
B
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoons)
Dry yeast: 1.4 g(½ small spoons)

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so
the dough is about 24°C after
kneading.

Method

1 Make the dough and give it its first rise
1 Fit the bread blade in the pan. Add A in this order: French
bread flour → malt powder → water.
2 Initial kneading: [Knead 2] 3 min. Leave in the pan to rest for
about 20 min.
3 Add B, keeping the salt and dry yeast apart. Knead again:
[Knead 2] 1 min → [Knead 3] 5 min → [Knead 4] 7 min (13
min total).
4 Round the dough and let rise on [Rise 3] for about 80 min.
Remove the dough from the pan and take out the bread blade.

2 Second rise
1 Press the dough firmly to release the gas. Fold into thirds
horizontally, then vertically, to bring it together. Return it to the
pan.
• If the dough is sticky and difficult to handle, use more dusting
flour.
2 [Rise 3]: about 80 min, until about twice its original size. Guide:
when you poke the centre with a floured finger, the hole should
shrink slightly but remain visible.

3 Shape
1 Remove the dough from the pan and divide into 2 with a
dough scraper. Cover with a cloth and rest at 20-25°C for about
20 minutes; do not let it dry out.
2 Shape each into a log 20-25 cm long (see p.28). Prove at
30-35°C for 40-60 minutes. Guide: a light finger press should
leave a slight indentation.

4 Bake
1 Score the dough and bake using your oven’s automatic
French bread program.

To set the temperature manually:
1 Score the dough, spray with water and bake in
a preheated oven at 180-200°C for about 30
minutes.

Olive Rye Rolls

Bake
1 Use kitchen scissors to make three
cross-shaped cuts in the dough. Brush
with olive oil.
2 Bake in a preheated oven at 190-210°C
for about 10 minutes.
3 Brush with olive oil again after baking.

Shape
1 Remove the dough from the pan and
press gently to release the gas. Divide into
14 with a dough scraper. Round into
smooth, taut balls. Rest at room
temperature for about 20 minutes; do not let
them dry out.
2 Press with your palm to form ovals.
3 Place 3 olives on each piece. Roll the
dough around them and shape.
4 Prove at 30-35°C for 10-30 minutes.

Method

Make the dough and give it its first rise
1 Fit the bread blade in the pan. Add A and
make the dough. [Knead 2] 4 min →
[Knead 3] 2 min → [Knead 4] 5 min (11
min total).
2 [Rise 3]: about 50 min.

Filling
Pitted olives: 42 pieces

To finish
Olive oil: as needed

steps.text:
Method

1 Make the dough and give it its first rise
1 Fit the bread blade in the pan. Add A and the poolish, and make the dough.
[Knead 1] 2 min → [Knead 3] 3 min → [Knead 4] 12 min (17 min total).
2 Remove the dough from the pan. Form a smooth, taut ball and put in a lightly oiled bowl.
3 Let rise at about 30°C for about 60 minutes.

2 Second rise
1 Remove the dough from the bowl and press gently by hand to
release the gas. Fold into thirds horizontally, then vertically, to
shape it. Return to the bowl.
2 Let rise at about 30°C for about 60 minutes.

3 Shape
1 Remove the dough from the bowl and divide into 2 with a dough scraper.
Round loaf: round into a smooth, taut ball.
Long loaf: fold from the far edge towards you to form a log about 10 cm long, with a
smooth, taut surface.

• Do not round too tightly.
2 Rest at 25-30°C for about 20 minutes; do not let the dough dry out.
3 Use plenty of dusting flour when shaping.
Round loaf: 1) Press all over with your palm to release the gas. Round into a smooth, taut ball,
pinching the bottom closed. 2) Coat the top with French bread flour and place flour-side down
in a cloth-lined rattan basket.
Long loaf: 1) Press all over with your palm to release the gas. Place smooth-side down, fold in
the far third and press together. 2) Turn 180 degrees, fold in the far third again and press
together. Fold in half and press firmly along the edge to seal (about 16 cm long). 3) Coat the
surface with flour. Lay a cloth on the board and form pleats; place the dough seam-side up
between them.
4 Prove at 30-35°C. Round loaf: about 60 min. Long loaf: about 60 min.

4 Bake
1 Preheat the oven with the baking tray inside.
2 Place the dough seam-side down on baking parchment and transfer it with the
parchment onto the tray.
3 Use a bread lame to score a lattice 1-2 mm deep. Spray with water.
4 Bake using your oven’s automatic French bread program (about 30 minutes).
To set the temperature manually:
1 Preheat the oven and tray to about 200°C. Bake for 30-35
minutes.
• If available, use steam for the first 3-5 minutes for greater volume and a glossy
surface.

• Adjust ingredient
temperatures so the dough
is about 26°C after kneading.

name: Bacon Épi

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Method

1 Make the dough and give it its first rise
1 Fit the bread blade in the pan. Add A and make the dough.
[Knead 1] 2 min → [Knead 3] 3 min → [Knead 4] 15 min (20
min total).
2 Remove the dough from the pan. Work in the coarsely
ground black pepper evenly. Round into a smooth, taut ball
and put in a lightly oiled bowl.
3 Let rise at about 30°C for about 50 minutes.

2 Shape
1 Remove the dough from the bowl and divide into 6 with a
dough scraper. Fold from the far edge towards you to form logs
about 6 cm long, with a smooth, taut underside.
2 Rest at 25-30°C for about 15 minutes; do not let them dry out.
3 Place seam-side up and roll out to the same length as the
bacon.
4 Spread with wholegrain mustard, lay on the bacon and roll
from the far edge towards you into a log. Seal the seam. •
Moisten the surface on a damp cloth, then coat with white poppy
seeds.
5 Place seam-side down on a baking tray. Hold scissors at 45
degrees and cut deeply, almost through. Move alternate
sections left and right to form a wheat-ear shape.
6 Prove at 30-35°C for about 40 minutes.
• Spray with water beforehand. If your appliance has a
steam function, use it.

3 Bake
1 Spray the surface with water.
2 Preheat the oven to 220°C, then reduce to about 200°C
and bake for 18-20 minutes.

• If available, use steam for the first 3 minutes for greater
volume and a glossy surface.

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Method

1 Make the dough and give it its first rise
1 Fit the bread blade in the pan. Add A and make the dough.
[Knead 1] 2 min → [Knead 3] 3 min → [Knead 4] 2 min (7 min total).
2 Remove the dough from the pan. Round into a smooth, taut ball and put in a lightly
oiled bowl.
3 Let rise at room temperature for 10-20 minutes.

2 Refrigerated rise
1 Put the dough in a plastic bag. Refrigerate at 3-5°C for 3-20 hours to rise.

3 Fold in the butter
1 Take the firm butter straight from the refrigerator. Tap with a rolling pin and roll to an
even thickness, forming a square about 15 × 15 cm.
2 Roll the dough into a square slightly larger than the butter.
3 Position the butter with its edges perpendicular to the dough’s diagonals. Fold the
surrounding dough towards the centre.
4 Pinch or overlap the seams and seal firmly so no butter escapes.
5 Roll to about 3 times the length (about 45 cm), then fold into thirds. Wrap in cling film
and rest in the freezer for 30-40 minutes.
• In warm conditions, such as summer, chill the dough frequently.
6 Repeat step 5 twice.

4 Shape
1 Roll the well-chilled dough to 18 × 50 cm, about 3 mm thick. If it will not roll out in one
go, chill in the freezer between attempts.
2 Cut 12 triangles with an 8 cm base and 18 cm height.
3 Chocolate croissants: point the tip towards you. Place chocolate at the base and roll
from the base towards you. Place on a tray with the tip underneath.
Plain croissants: point the tip towards you. Roll from the base towards you. Place on a
baking tray with the tip underneath.
4 Prove at 25-30°C for 60-70 minutes.

• Spray with water beforehand. If your appliance has a steam function,
use it.
5 Bake
1 Brush with beaten egg.
2 Preheat the oven to 220°C, then reduce to about 180°C and
bake for about 15 minutes.

Method

1 Make the dough
1 Fit the bread blade in the pan. Add A and make the dough.
[Knead 1] 2 min → [Knead 3] 3 min → [Knead 4] 5 min
(10 min total).
2 Refrigerated rise
1 Remove the dough from the pan and round lightly. Put in a plastic bag and refrigerate
at 3-5°C for 8-24 hours to rise.

3 Fold in the butter
1 Remove the dough from the refrigerator. Roll slightly larger than the laminating butter.

5 Prove at 30-35°C for 50-70 minutes, until about 1.5 times the original size.

5 Bake
1 Brush with beaten egg and prick
the base in several places with a
fork.
2 Bake in a preheated oven at

name: Plain Bagels

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Plain Bagels

Ingredients (makes 6)
165 kcal(per piece)
A

French bread flour: 250 g
Butter: 5 g
Sugar: 8.5 g(1 large spoons)
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoons)
Water: 170 g(mL)
Dry yeast: 2.8 g(1 small spoons)

For boiling
Hot water: as needed
Sugar (2–3% per litre of
water): as needed

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so the dough is about 28°C after
kneading.

Topping
Shredded cheese: as
needed

Method

Make the dough / first rise
① Fit the kneading blade and put A in the bread pan.
② [Knead 1] 2 minutes → [Knead 3] 2 minutes → [Knead 4]
15 minutes (19 minutes total).
③ [Rise 3] for about 30 minutes, until 1.5 times its original
size. Remove the dough and kneading blade.

Second rise
④ Press out the gas firmly. Fold into thirds horizontally
and vertically, round, and return to the bread pan.
⑤ [Rise 3] for about 20 minutes, then remove.

Shape
⑥ Place on a canvas cloth, divide into 6 and round
lightly. Flatten with your palm, then roll out with a rolling
pin.
⑦ Fold the top third in, turn the dough around and fold
the other third in.
⑧ Fold in half from the folded edge, make a long shape
and seal the seam to form a 20 cm log.
⑨ With the seam up, flatten one fifth of one end into a
flap. Form a ring, wrap the flap around the other end, and
seal on the inside of the ring.

• Seal firmly, or the join may open before baking.
• Make the hole about the size of your thumb. A taut surface
gives a neat shape.
⑩ Prove the 6 bagels in an oven at 25–30°C for about 20
minutes, until the holes become slightly smaller.

Boil
⑪ Heat water with sugar to about 90°C. Boil the bagels
for about 1 minute on each side, drain well and space out
on a baking tray.

Bake
⑫ Bake in an oven at 180–200°C for about 20
minutes.

Sesame & Cheese Bagels

Ingredients (makes 6)
209 kcal(per piece)
A

French bread flour: 250 g
Butter: 5 g
Sugar: 8.5 g(1 large spoons)
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoons)
Water: 170 g(mL)
Dry yeast: 2.8 g(1 small spoons)
Black sesame seeds: 10 g

• Adjust water temperatures so the
dough is about 28°C after kneading.

Follow the method for plain bagels.
Sprinkle with shredded cheese before
baking.

Topping
Shredded cheese: as
needed

Method

Make the dough / first rise
① Fit the kneading blade and put A in the bread pan.
② [Knead 1] 2 minutes → [Knead 3] 2 minutes → [Knead 4]
15 minutes (19 minutes total).
③ [Rise 3] for about 30 minutes, until 1.5 times its original
size. Remove the dough and kneading blade.

Second rise
④ Press out the gas firmly. Fold into thirds horizontally
and vertically, round, and return to the bread pan.
⑤ [Rise 3] for about 20 minutes, then remove.

Shape
⑥ Place on a canvas cloth, divide into 6 and round
lightly. Flatten with your palm, then roll out with a rolling
pin.
⑦ Fold the top third in, turn the dough around and fold
the other third in.
⑧ Fold in half from the folded edge, make a long shape
and seal the seam to form a 20 cm log.
⑨ With the seam up, flatten one fifth of one end into a
flap. Form a ring, wrap the flap around the other end, and
seal on the inside of the ring.

• Seal firmly, or the join may open before baking.
• Make the hole about the size of your thumb. A taut surface
gives a neat shape.
⑩ Prove the 6 bagels in an oven at 25–30°C for about 20
minutes, until the holes become slightly smaller.

Boil
⑪ Heat water with sugar to about 90°C. Boil the bagels
for about 1 minute on each side, drain well and space out
on a baking tray.

Bake
⑫ Bake in an oven at 180–200°C for about 20
minutes.

Doughnuts

Ingredients (four 8 cm rings)
173 kcal (per piece)
A

Bread flour: 200 g
Cake flour: 50 g
Skimmed milk powder: 12 g(2
large spoons)
Water: 120 g(mL)
Dry yeast: 2.8 g(1 small spoons)
Flavourings (vanilla, lemon,
nutmeg, etc.): as desired
Oil for frying: as needed

Creamed mixture
Butter (at room temperature): 30 g
Sugar: 30 g (3½ large spoons)
Egg yolk: 20 g
Salt: 5 g (1 small spoon)

Vanilla sugar: as needed

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so the
dough is about 28°C after kneading.

Method

Make the dough
① Fit the kneading blade. Put A and the creamed mixture in
the bread pan.
② [Knead 1] 2 minutes → [Knead 3] 3 minutes → [Knead 4] 15
minutes (20 minutes total).
③ Remove, shape into a taut ball and place in an oiled bowl.
Prove at 25–30°C for about 50 minutes. Do not let it dry out.

Shape
④ Remove from the bowl onto a canvas cloth. Roll into an 18
× 18 cm square, 1.5 cm thick. Cover with plastic wrap and
rest at room temperature for 5–10 minutes. Do not let it dry
out.
⑤ Cut out rings using 8 cm and 3 cm cutters.
⑥ Prove at 30–35°C for about 35 minutes. (Use the scraps
for Berliner Krapfen.)

• Mist with water or use steam to prevent drying.

Fry
⑦ Fry in oil at 170–180°C for 1–1½ minutes on each side.
Drain and cool, then coat with vanilla sugar or other toppings.

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Berliner Krapfen
(using doughnut scraps)

① Put the butter and sugar in a bowl and beat with a hand mixer to
incorporate air.
② When pale, add the egg yolk and salt and beat until the mixture no
longer drips from the whisk.

Making the creamed
mixture

Method

Shape
① Divide the doughnut scraps into 4 and round until fairly
smooth. Cover with plastic wrap and rest at room
temperature for 5–10 minutes. Do not let them dry out.
② Press out the gas with your palm, round into taut balls and
rest on a cloth for 5–10 minutes.
③ Press flat with a board. Prove at 30–35°C for about 50
minutes.

• Mist with water or use steam to prevent drying.

Fry
④ Fry in oil at 170–180°C for 1–1½ minutes on each side.
Drain. While still warm, make a hole in the side with a
chopstick.
⑤ Put jam in a piping bag with a narrow nozzle and pipe
into the hole. Coat with vanilla sugar.

Ingredients (makes 4)
196 kcal(per piece)
Dough left after cutting out
the doughnuts
Vanilla sugar: as needed
Jam (raspberry, etc.): as needed

steps.text:
Dough [d3] Enriched dough
Enriched Dough

Ingredients

Bread flour: 280 g
Butter: 50 g
Sugar: 25.5 g (3 large spoons)
Skimmed milk powder: 12 g (2 large spoons)
Salt: 5 g (1 small spoon)
Egg (beaten): 25 g (½ medium egg)
Water: 140 g (mL)
Dry yeast: 2.8 g (1 small spoon)

* At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use cold
water (about 5°C).

Use high-protein Japanese bread flour (11% or more).
Commercially available Japanese wheat flour gives a chewy, springy texture.

• Bread may rise less than bread made with Nisshin Seifun Welna “Camellia”. If the baked bread is at least 10 cm high (7 cm for quick bread), there
is no problem.
• Results may vary with the flour brand (variety) and harvest year.

name: Pain de campagne (without poolish)

steps.title: Documented recipe and method
steps.text:
Program 11: French bread
Pain de campagne
(made with poolish)

Ingredients
900kcal

Poolish (pre-ferment)
<A>
Water (about 25°C) ... 100g(mL)
Dry yeast ... 0.7g(¼ small spoon)
Bread flour ... 100g

<B>
Bread flour ... 100g
Wholemeal flour ... 50g
Salt ... 5g(1 small spoon)
Cold water (5°C) * ... 90g(mL)

Dry yeast ... 1.4g(½ small spoon)

* At room temperatures of 25°C or
above, reduce the amount by 10 g
(mL).
Using a poolish takes a little more effort, but produces an authentic
pain de campagne. Do not use the delay timer when using a poolish.
For a simpler version, use the quantities given for the recipe without
poolish.

Without poolish (pre-ferment)

Bread flour ... 200g
Wholemeal flour ... 50g
Salt ... 5g(1 small spoon)
Cold water (5°C) * ... 190g(mL)
Dry yeast ... 1.4g(½ small spoon)

* At room temperatures of 25°C or
above, reduce the amount by 10 g
(mL).

Fit the kneading blade in the bread
pan and add all ingredients except
the dry yeast. Put the dry yeast in the
yeast dispenser. Select Program 11
and press Start.

Method

1 Make the poolish (pre-ferment)
① Put the water and dry yeast in a bowl and whisk to dissolve.
② Add the bread flour and mix with a rubber spatula until smooth,
with no dry flour remaining. The finished poolish should be 20–30°C.
③ Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a plastic bag. Leave at room
temperature for 60 minutes, then refrigerate for 8–18 hours.

2 Bake using Program 11
① Fit the kneading blade in the bread pan. Add B and the poolish A,
then place the pan in the machine.
② Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser, select Program 11 and press
Start.

3 Remove the loaf
Lay a towel underneath. Move your hands firmly downwards,
tapping against the work surface to release the bread. See
“French bread” in the instruction manual.

1 Make the poolish (pre-ferment)
① Put the water and dry yeast in a bowl and whisk to dissolve.
② Add the bread flour and mix with a rubber spatula until smooth,
with no dry flour remaining. The finished poolish should be 20–30°C.
③ Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a plastic bag. Leave at room
temperature for 60 minutes, then refrigerate for 8–18 hours.

2 Bake using Program 11
① Fit the kneading blade in the bread pan. Add B and the poolish A,
then place the pan in the machine.
② Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser, select Program 11 and press
Start.

3 Remove the loaf
Lay a towel underneath. Move your hands firmly downwards,
tapping against the work surface to release the bread. See
“French bread” in the instruction manual.

Croissants

Can be made with enriched dough or natural yeast bread dough.

Dough d3: Rich dough

Ingredients (12 croissants) • With dry
yeast 201 kcal each

A

Bread flour: 225 g
Cake flour: 55 g
Butter: 15 g
Sugar: 25.5 g(3 large spoons)
Skim milk powder: 6 g(1 large spoon)
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoon)
Egg (beaten): 25 g(½ medium egg)
Water: 140 g(mL)

Dry yeast: 2.8 g (1 small spoon)
Butter for laminating (cut into 1 cm-
thick slices): 140 g

To finish
Egg wash (beaten egg): 25 g (½ medium egg)

Dough d4: Natural yeast dough

• With natural yeast
204 kcal each

A

Prepared natural yeast starter: 25 g(2
large spoons)
Bread flour: 230 g
Cake flour: 50 g
Butter: 15 g
Sugar: 25.5 g(3 large spoons)
Skim milk powder: 6 g(1 large spoon)
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoon)
Egg (beaten): 25 g(½ medium egg)
Water: 120 g(mL)

Butter for laminating (cut into 1
cm-thick slices): 140 g

To finish
Egg wash (beaten egg): 25 g (½ medium egg)

Method

1
Make the dough
With dry yeast: make enriched dough using dough program d3 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry yeast in the yeast
dispenser and make the dough.
With natural yeast: make natural yeast bread dough using dough program d4 (see
manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add the prepared starter, then A. Make the
dough.

2
Laminate with butter
① Remove the dough, place in a bowl, cover with cling film and refrigerate
for 30–60 minutes (longer in a warm room).
② Dust the laminating butter with flour, arrange the slices together, wrap in
cling film and roll into a square about 20 × 20 cm. Refrigerate for 15–30
minutes.
③ Press the dough with tapping motions of the rolling pin, then roll into a
square about 30 × 30 cm.
④ Place the butter from ② on the dough and enclose it. Wrap in cling film
and refrigerate for 10–20 minutes.
⑤ Tap with the rolling pin and, once slightly thinner, roll flat.
⑥ Fold into thirds, wrap in cling film and refrigerate for 10–20 minutes.
⑦ Repeat ⑤ and ⑥ twice more, then chill for 30–60 minutes.

3
Shape
① Divide into 2 with a scraper. Roll each piece into a rectangle about 18 ×
40 cm and cut into 6 isosceles triangles.
② Roll up while pulling the ends.
③ Arrange seam-side down.
④ Mist with water, cover with cling film and prove at room temperature for
40–60 minutes, until about twice the size.

4
Bake
① Brush with egg wash and bake in a preheated oven at 200–220°C for
about 10 minutes. Refrigerate the remaining dough to prevent
overproving.
